FOR DEMOCRACY!!!!!
This game makes every failure seem like a success and as a professional failure, this is exactly what I needed.

FOR DEMOCRACY!!! 

The action is no-stop, every combat scenario is like it's out of Saving Private Ryan. Fighting the bots feels like a torrential downpour of laser fire, the bugs are a never ending horde of pain. The amount of great laughs I've had with friends is too much to count. 

If you have friends to play with it's a no-brainier. 

Disclosure: This game was not on my radar, when I first saw game-play I thought meh then my friend got it for me and my mind was changed after about 30 minutes.

Ugh absolutely the most Starship Troopers game since Starship troopers came out. Difficult at higher levels, easy on low levels and fairly well balanced PVE-COOP. Solo is difficult but not impossible even on level 5+. Graphics 9/10 as there can be intense flares of light from even just lamp posts in small bases. Sound is perfect. Gameplay is intense at all levels of play barring easy mode.

A sense of devotion is felt as soon as you load the game up. The intro cinematic, the music, the animations, the propaganda all work together to make you feel patriotic and ready to lead your fellow helldivers ahead to install managed democracy amongst the stars. Absolutely do not pass this game up.

FOR DEMOCRACY! 

*Note: This review was provided by the Ministry of Truth.

Game appears to be pretty damn fun and the graphics are beautiful. That being said, the anti-cheat software they decided to use in this game is probably one the worst. I've known about it for a long time as it was used in a popular Asian MMO I used to play for years. Even in under an hour, the anti-cheat software managed to close two programs I really need to use on my PC, and they don't interact with the game at all yet this software decided to control my PC and close them. The fact that they  decided to go with this specific one is really bizarre to me, but oh well. Though... I don't think the software is as dangerous as people claim it to be, however it does like to control specific things on your PC without your immediate, direct consent. As is pretty commonly talked about when you look this anti-cheat software up, it does [b]indeed[/b] not fully uninstall I've found. It will remain and do things. There is legitimately zero [i]good[/i] reason for this. If it were about whether or not the user is going to re-install a game that utilizes that same anti-cheat, then the files should remain dormant, not running, until that condition is met. But that is not the case here for who knows what reason. If you don't particularly care about a game's anti-cheat potentially going behind your back and closing things just because it wants to, then by all means get the game and enjoy it, because it's a great game. Otherwise, don't even try it because the software will hook itself in and you'll have to research the potentially long process of scrubbing it from your OS. Only real way I'm going to pick this game back up is if a friend really wanted to play it together because we'd have fun, I'd just have to deal with the anti-cheat closing things randomly.
